tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Masterminds Workshop Site is a Next.js 16 application that serves as a platform for event marketing, registration, and content distribution. It enables Joe Che to run live workshops (both online and in-person), distribute giveaways and lead magnets, collect attendee information, and manage payment processing through Stripe. The site integrates with Supabase for data persistence, Resend for email delivery, and multiple third-party services for automation and tracking. Key audience: workshop attendees, giveaway consumers, lead magnet prospects. Core flows: discover event → register → pay → receive follow-ups.

tour.title: Event System Architecture
tour.description: The event system is the centerpiece of the platform. Events are configured in a central registry (src/lib/events.ts) and exposed through two main pages: the events index page lists upcoming events with pricing and modality info, while individual event detail pages provide full event info, registration forms, and checkout. Events support flexible pricing (free, fixed, donations), multiple formats (online via Zoom, in-person, hybrid), and optional promo codes. Each event can have capacity limits (seat tracking), post-purchase setup instructions, and automated email sequences. The system tracks attendee acquisition source (utm params, referrers, specific campaigns).

tour.title: Payment & Registration Flow
tour.description: When an attendee submits the registration form, the client-side form handler calls the POST /api/events/checkout-session route. This route validates the attendee's input (name, email, WhatsApp number, business context), checks rate limits, resolves any promo code, calculates the final charge amount, claims an event capacity seat, and creates a Stripe Checkout Session with proper metadata. The response includes the sessionId for the client to redirect to Stripe. The checkout session is attached to the seat reservation, so if the checkout expires, the seat is automatically released. After payment, the flow continues with post-purchase setup (if configured) or follow-up emails.

tour.title: Payment Verification & Webhooks
tour.description: Stripe webhooks provide server-side certainty that payment succeeded, even if the client browser crashes after checkout. The /api/stripe/webhook route listens for three event types: checkout.session.completed (payment succeeded), checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded (deferred payment cleared), and checkout.session.expired (checkout timed out without payment). On success, the webhook finalizes the registration (records it in Supabase, marks the seat as confirmed, triggers follow-up emails). On expiration, the reserved seat is released so others can book. This webhook-first architecture prevents double-bookings and ensures no attendee falls through the cracks due to network failures.

tour.title: Lead Magnets & Giveaways System
tour.description: Lead magnets are free content assets (downloads, quizzes, guides) distributed in exchange for email addresses. The giveaways system has two layers: (1) pack-based giveaways under /giveaways/<slug> which use a template page component with structured content (sections, guides, troubleshooting), and (2) lead magnet routes at /api/lead-magnets/<source> that handle email capture and delivery. A user finds a giveaway, views the content, and optionally subscribes to email. The /api/lead-magnet route is the unified ingestion point that accepts source, email, and giveaway slug, then routes to the appropriate builder (generic giveaway email, free AI tool email, quiz giveaway email, etc.) and delivers via Resend with proper list-unsubscribe headers and suppression checks.

tour.title: Post-Purchase Experience & Attendee Setup
tour.description: After an attendee pays for an event, they are redirected to the setup page (/events/<slug>/setup) which guides them through pre-event preparation. The setup page is configured per-event and may include primary and secondary action items (e.g., 'Install this tool' or 'Review this guide'). The page is entirely configured in the event definition and can be omitted if no setup is needed. Additionally, the system sends a series of confirmation and reminder emails: immediate confirmation after payment, abandoned checkout recovery (for carts left unpaid), and pre-event reminders with timing information converted to the attendee's local timezone (Singapore, Europe, New York, Los Angeles). The event-confirmation-email module handles all these templates with consistent branding.

tour.title: Data Persistence & Tracking
tour.description: The system uses Supabase (PostgreSQL) as the primary data store for: event registrations (who attended which event and paid how much), event registration intake forms (detailed attendee info like WhatsApp, business context), event email ledger (which emails were sent to whom), and giveaway subscriptions (email signups via lead magnets). Registrations and intakes are saved during the checkout flow; the email ledger is updated as confirmation and follow-up emails are sent. For analytics, the system tracks user interactions via the 'insight-to-fix' tracking system (checkout_failed, stripe_webhook events, etc.). Event seat capacity is managed in-memory per server instance during checkout but also reflected in the database for durability. This layered approach ensures no concurrent bookings exceed event capacity.

tour.title: Discovery, SEO & Content Distribution
tour.description: The sitemap.ts file defines all discoverable URLs and their priority/change frequency for search engines. All event pages, giveaway pages, lead magnet pages, and bonus content are enumerated with proper metadata. Individual event pages include OpenGraph and Twitter card metadata so they preview correctly on social media. The giveaway system is a content hub driving organic traffic and lead capture; each giveaway page is optimized for a specific keyword or use case and linked from the sitemap. The free-ai-tools subsystem generates a giveaway page per tool (AI-agent-income, Claude MD, chat-to-flowchart, etc.), each with consistent templates. Canonical URLs are set to prevent duplication. This architecture makes the site highly discoverable and shareable.
